1.q: וַ⁠יָּבֹ֣אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל כָּל־הָ֨⁠עֵדָ֤ה מִדְבַּר־צִן֙ בַּ⁠חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽ⁠רִאשׁ֔וֹן
1.note: The author is using the word translated as **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
See how you translated these same phrases in Numbers 1:2. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

This is the first month of the Hebrew calendar. It marks when God rescued the Israelites from the Egyptians. The first month is during the last part of March and the first part of April on the Western calendar.

Here the author implies that this is the **first month** of the fortieth year since the Israelites left the land of Egypt. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [in the first month of the year that was forty years after they left Egypt]
The word “Zin” here is the Hebrew name of the wilderness.
The phrase **the people** refers to the sons of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the Israelites dwelt]

The expression **she was buried** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they buried her there]

2.note: Here the author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

Here, the author implies that **there was no water** in or near the city of Kadesh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could make that explicit. Alternate translation: [And there was no water in Kadesh]
The pronoun **they** refers to the congregation. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the congregation assembled]
The pronoun **they** refers to the congregation. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the congregation assembled]

3.note: Here and throughout the chapter, the term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

The people are using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling, a desperate wish that they had already died. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [We would rather have died]

By **we**, the people mean themselves and their fellow Israelites but not those to whom they are speaking, so use the exclusive form of that word in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The people are referring to death in a polite way by using the phrase **we had expired when our brothers expired**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [we had died when our brothers died]

Here the people are speaking as if their fellow Israelites were their brothers. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [our kinsmen]

Here, to the face of Yahweh represents being in Yahweh’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

4.q: וְ⁠לָ⁠מָ֤ה הֲבֵאתֶם֙ אֶת קְהַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה אֶל הַ⁠מִּדְבָּ֖ר הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה לָ⁠מ֣וּת שָׁ֔ם אֲנַ֖חְנוּ וּ⁠בְעִירֵֽ⁠נוּ
4.note: Here, the word **to** marks **die there** as the purpose of **have you brought the assembly of Yahweh to this wilderness**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

4.q: וְ⁠לָ⁠מָ֤ה הֲבֵאתֶם֙ אֶת־קְהַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הַ⁠מִּדְבָּ֖ר הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה לָ⁠מ֣וּת שָׁ֔ם
4.note: The people are using the question form to rebuke Moses and Aaron for bringing them into the wilderness to die. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have brought the assembly of Yahweh to this wilderness to die there!]
The pronoun **you** refers to Moses and Aaron. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [have Moses and Aaron brought]

The people are using the possessive form to describe an **assembly** that is characterized by belonging to **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the assembly that worships Yahweh]

By **we**, the people mean themselves and their fellow Israelites but not those to whom they are speaking, so use the exclusive form of that word in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

5.q: וְ⁠לָ⁠מָ֤ה הֶֽעֱלִיתֻ֨⁠נוּ֙ מִ⁠מִּצְרַ֔יִם לְ⁠הָבִ֣יא אֹתָ֔⁠נוּ אֶל הַ⁠מָּק֥וֹם הָ⁠רָ֖ע הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה לֹ֣א מְק֣וֹם זֶ֗רַע וּ⁠תְאֵנָ֤ה וְ⁠גֶ֨פֶן֙ וְ⁠רִמּ֔וֹן וּ⁠מַ֥יִם אַ֖יִן לִ⁠שְׁתּֽוֹת
5.note: Here, the word **to** marks **bring us to this evil place** as the purpose of **did you bring us up from Egypt**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

5.q: וְ⁠לָ⁠מָ֤ה הֶֽעֱלִיתֻ֨⁠נוּ֙ מִ⁠מִּצְרַ֔יִם לְ⁠הָבִ֣יא אֹתָ֔⁠נוּ אֶל הַ⁠מָּק֥וֹם הָ⁠רָ֖ע הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה
5.note: The people are using the question form to rebuke Moses and Aaron for bringing them up out of Egypt to this evil place. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not have brought us up from Egypt to bring us to this evil place!]

6.note: Here, **from the face of the assembly** represents being in front of the assembly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [away from the assembly]
The pronouns **they** and **their** refer to Moses and Aaron. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Moses and Aaron fell on their faces]

Moses is using the possessive form to describe the **glory** that is characterized by belonging to **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the divine glory]

Here, **the glory of Yahweh** represents a visible display of Yahweh himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh himself appeared]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the glorious Yahweh]

8.note: Here, the staff could be: (1) the staff with Aaron’s name on it from Numbers 17. That was the staff that budded and produced almonds, which proved that Aaron was the priest that Yahweh had chosen. Alternate translation: [Aaron’s staff that budded] (2) the staff that Moses used when he performed miracles in Egypt. Alternate translation: [your staff] or [the staff that you used in Egypt]
The pronoun **their** refers to the congregation. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and you shall speak to the rock while the congregation watches]

Yahweh is using to their eyes as a common expression of the culture to mean “in their sight.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in their sight]

Yahweh is speaking of the rock as if it were a living thing that could **give its water**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and water will flow from it]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the **water** that is characterized by coming from the rock. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the water it holds]

9.note: Here, **from before the face of Yahweh** represents being in Yahweh’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from Yahweh’s presence]
The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh, and the pronoun **him** refers to Moses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [just as Yahweh commanded him]

10.note: The author is using **to the face of the rock** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in front of the rock.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [before the rock]
The pronoun **he** refers to Moses, and the pronoun **them** refers to the assembly. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Moses said to the assembly]

Moses is using the adjective **rebellious** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [you rebellious people]

10.q: הֲ⁠מִן הַ⁠סֶּ֣לַע הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה נוֹצִ֥יא לָ⁠כֶ֖ם מָֽיִם
10.note: Moses is using the question form to express his frustration and doubt about bringing water out of the rock for the people. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [From this rock we can actually bring out water for you!]
By **we**, Moses means himself and Aaron but not the people to whom he is speaking, so use the exclusive form of that word in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

11.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the congregation drank, and their livestock drank too]

12.note: The pronoun **you** refers to Moses and Aaron. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the two of you did not believe]

Yahweh is using **to the eyes of the sons of Israel** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in the sight of the sons of Israel.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [before the sons of Israel]
The pronoun **them** refers to the sons of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [that I have given to the sons of Israel]

13.note: Here the author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

Here, the pronoun them could refer to: (1) the Israelites. In this case, Yahweh showed that he is holy to the Israelites. Alternate translation: [among the Israelites] (2) the waters. In this case, Yahweh used the waters to show that he is holy. Alternate translation: [through the waters]

14.note: The author is using the word translated as **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
The phrase **Thus says your brother Israel** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

14.q: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אָחִ֣י⁠ךָ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַ⁠תְּלָאָ֖ה
14.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Your brother Israel says that you know all of the hardship]

Here the people of Israel are speaking as if their nation were the **brother** of the king of Edom, because the two nations descended from the brothers Jacob and Esau. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the nation descended from your brother Jacob]
The pronoun **your** refers to the king of Edom. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Edom’s brother Israel]

The people of Israel are speaking of **the hardship** as if it were a living thing that could find them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the hardship we have experienced]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **hardship**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the trouble]

15.note: Here the people of Israel are speaking as if their ancestors were their literal fathers. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [our forefathers]

By **we**, the people of Israel mean themselves and their ancestors but not the king of Edom to whom they are speaking, so use the exclusive form of that word in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

16.note: By **we**, **our**, and **us**, the people of Israel mean themselves and their ancestors but not the king of Edom to whom they are speaking, so use the exclusive form of those words in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The pronoun **he**, used three times here, refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh heard our voice, and Yahweh sent a messenger, and Yahweh brought us out]

Here, **our voice** represents the cry for help that the people of Israel called out. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and he heard our plea]

Here, the messenger could be: (1) an angel that Yahweh sent to help the Israelites. Alternate translation: [an angel] (2) a human representative, probably Moses. Alternate translation: [a representative]

Here the people of Israel are speaking as if there were something for the king of Edom to look at, using the word **behold** to focus his attention on what they say next. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And so now]

17.note: By **We**, the people of Israel mean themselves but not the king of Edom to whom they are speaking, so use the exclusive form of that word in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The people of Israel are using the possessive form to describe **water** that is characterized by coming from a **well**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [water from a well]

The people of Israel are using the possessive form to describe a **way** that is characterized by belonging to the **king**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [on the royal road]

The people of Israel are referring to all possible directions by naming two major components, the **right** and the **left**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [We will not turn aside in any direction]

18.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָי⁠ו֙ אֱד֔וֹם לֹ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר בִּ֑⁠י פֶּן בַּ⁠חֶ֖רֶב אֵצֵ֥א לִ⁠קְרָאתֶֽ⁠ךָ
18.note: Here, the word **lest** marks **with the sword I come out to meet you** as the outcome that the king of Edom warns will happen if the Israelites try to pass through. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that avoiding this outcome is the purpose of his warning.

Here, **Edom** represents the king of Edom, its ruler, who is speaking on the nation’s behalf. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the king of Edom said to him]
The pronoun **me** refers to Edom and its land. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [You shall not pass over my land]

Here, **the sword** represents military force or armed attack. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [with my armed forces]

19.q: וְ⁠אִם מֵימֶ֤י⁠ךָ נִשְׁתֶּה֙ אֲנִ֣י וּ⁠מִקְנַ֔⁠י וְ⁠נָתַתִּ֖י מִכְרָ֑⁠ם
19.note: The people of Israel are presenting a possible condition, that they will pay for any water that they or their livestock drink. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [And if we or our livestock drink your water, then we will pay for it]
The pronoun **I** refers to the people of Israel, speaking as a single group. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I, all Israel, and my livestock]
The pronoun **its** refers to the water. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [then I will give the price of the water I drank]

The people of Israel are using **on my feet** as a common expression of the culture to mean “on foot” or “by walking.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [walking]

20.note: The pronoun **he** refers to the king of Edom. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The king of Edom said]

Here, **Edom** represents the people of Edom. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And the Edomites came out to meet him]

Here, **a strong hand** represents great military power. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and with a powerful army]

21.q: וַ⁠יְמָאֵ֣ן אֱד֗וֹם נְתֹן֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֲבֹ֖ר בִּ⁠גְבֻל֑⁠וֹ וַ⁠יֵּ֥ט יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל & מֵ⁠עָלָֽי⁠ו
21.note: Here, **Edom** represents the Edomite king and his people, and **Israel** represents the Israelites. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The Edomite king and his people refused to give the Israelites to pass over in their border. And the Israelites turned aside from upon them.]
The pronouns **his** and **him** refer to Edom. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in Edom’s territory … away from Edom]

The author is using **turned aside from upon him** as a common expression of the culture to mean that Israel went away from Edom. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Israel went away from him]

22.note: The author is using the word translated as **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
The pronoun **they** refers to the sons of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the Israelites set out]

23.note: Moses is using the possessive form to describe a **border** that is characterized by being part of the **land of Edom**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the border next to Edom]

24.q: יֵאָסֵ֤ף אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל עַמָּ֔י⁠ו כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָבֹא֙ אֶל הָ⁠אָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַ֛ל אֲשֶׁר מְרִיתֶ֥ם אֶת פִּ֖⁠י לְ⁠מֵ֥י מְרִיבָֽה
24.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Aaron will be gathered to his peoples because he will not come to the land that I have given to the sons of Israel, since you rebelled against my mouth at the waters of Meribah]

The expression **will be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Aaron will join his ancestors]

Yahweh is referring to Aaron’s death in a polite way by using the phrase **will be gathered to his peoples**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [Aaron will die and join his ancestors]

Yahweh is using **my mouth** to represent the commands that he spoke. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you disobeyed my commands]
The pronoun **you** refers to Moses and Aaron. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Moses and Aaron rebelled against]

26.note: The expression **will be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Aaron will join his ancestors and die there]

Yahweh is referring to death in a polite way by using the phrase **will be gathered**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [And Aaron will die there]

27.note: The pronoun **they** refers to Moses, Aaron, and Eleazar. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Moses, Aaron, and Eleazar went up]

The author is using **to the eyes of all the congregation** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in the sight of all the congregation.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [while all the congregation watched]

29.q: וַ⁠יִּרְאוּ֙ כָּל הָ֣⁠עֵדָ֔ה כִּ֥י גָוַ֖ע אַהֲרֹ֑ן
29.note: The phrase **all the congregation** refers to all the people of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And all the people of Israel saw that Aaron expired]

Moses is referring to death in a polite way by using the word **expired**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [Aaron died]

Here, **all the house of Israel** represents the entire people of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the Israelites]

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **house** that is characterized by belonging to **Israel**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the Israelites]
